requirements.summary: 2 GHz dual-core · 6 GB RAM · 25 GB disk · 8 GB USB
requirements.note: Canonical's figures for the desktop: a 2 GHz dual-core processor, 6 GB RAM and 25 GB of free disk for a comfortable experience; below that it points at Xubuntu or Lubuntu. The installation medium needs an 8 GB stick or larger.

page.description: Ubuntu editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: Canonical's long-term-support release, on a five-year security clock. Pick Desktop or Server, then the architecture of the machine that will run it.
pros: Five years of free security updates: the LTS is supported until April 2031.
GNOME 50 desktop and Linux 7.0 on the same 26.04.1 media.
Server images for amd64, arm64, ppc64el, s390x and RISC-V in the same release.
One installer family and one set of release notes for desktop and server.
cons: Desktop wants 6 GB RAM and 25 GB of free disk; below that Canonical recommends Xubuntu or Lubuntu.
The 26.10 interim is newer, but it is supported for nine months, not five years.
The erase-disk option takes the entire selected drive; keeping another system means manual partitioning.
Writing the stick erases it, and the running system's own disk appears in the same device list.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of Ubuntu 16.04 with the Unity desktop from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 26.04 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: Ubuntu 16.04 Unity desktop with Files, a terminal and LibreOffice open
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of Ubuntu 16.04 (Unity) · not 26.04, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: Two official paths: the Desktop and Server ISOs, written to an 8 GB or larger stick with Disks, Startup Disk Creator or dd. Writing erases the stick; the installer's erase-disk option erases the target disk.

editions.name: Desktop
editions.description: The GNOME desktop Canonical ships, with the installer on the same ISO: try it live, then install or repartition.
editions.usbNote: 8 GB stick or larger. Disks (Restore Disk Image), Startup Disk Creator or dd; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Server
editions.description: The same release without a desktop: the live server installer for machines that are administered over SSH or a console.
editions.usbNote: Bootable on amd64 and arm64. The ppc64el, s390x and RISC-V images target their own firmware and hypervisors, not a PC USB stick.
